s05.title: Why copper fails past 3 m at 48Gbps
s05.left_body: Ultra High Speed HDMI carries 48Gbps. Signal loss in copper grows with frequency and with length, so a passive copper cable past about 3 m cannot carry 8K at 60Hz or 4K at 120Hz cleanly. The fix is either active electronics at each end or fiber. A hybrid active optical cable puts the video on fiber cores and keeps thin copper conductors for power and control signals.
s05.left_rule: Accurate wording: fiber optic HDMI, hybrid active optical. Never pure fiber or all glass.
table_rows: 7 m to 50 m in the current line
Thin and light, pulls through conduit
Directional: SOURCE and DISPLAY ends (our direction proof design)
s05.footnote: Length limits are a management summary of the HDMI specification; the brief's statement is that copper physically fails past 3 meters at 48Gbps.
s05.notes: The whole strategy rests on one physical fact: at 48Gbps passive copper stops working at about 3 m. Above that length the buyer needs active electronics or fiber, and that is where price competition with commodity copper disappears. The direction sensitivity of active cables is a real drawback that our direction proof design turns into a selling point.

s10.title: Five differentiators

cards.head: Direction proof design
cards.body: Color coded SOURCE and DISPLAY ends, printed arrows, QR code to a setup video. Lever 3: returns from 3% toward 2%.

cards.head: 5 Year Signal Guarantee
cards.body: The replacement ships before the return arrives. Simple promise, simple process (flowchart 04).

cards.head: CL3 in wall rating
cards.body: Claimed only after the factory's CL3 documentation is in hand. Opens the installer segment.

cards.head: Detachable head for conduit pulls
cards.body: The small head passes through conduit, then the connector clicks on. Installers ask for this first.

cards.head: Spec Match finder and trade up registration
cards.body: Buyers register for the guarantee and get a length and spec check. Builds the off Amazon email list (lever 11).

s10.notes: Each differentiator is tied to a number in the model or to a channel. The direction proof design moves the return rate, the guarantee and the registration build the email list that feeds the DTC channel in Year 3, and CL3 plus the detachable head open the installer channel in Year 2. None of them require new tooling beyond the factory's existing line, pending confirmation.

s13.title: US entity and tax

cards.head: Wyoming single member LLC
items: {wy_form} to form, about {wy_annual} per year, no state income tax, strong privacy.
Delaware costs about {de_annual} per year and is only worth it for raising investment.
BOI reporting is not required for US formed companies (FinCEN exemption finalized August 11, 2026).
EIN by phone or fax with Form SS-4, no SSN needed. Exact legal name match across state, IRS, bank and Amazon.

cards.head: Annual filing
items: A foreign owned single member LLC files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 every year.
Penalty for missing it: {penalty_5472}.
Wyoming annual report about {wy_annual}.
California may assert income tax nexus from FBA inventory: on the CPA list.

cards.head: Treaty position
items: 1976 US Korea tax treaty: business profits are taxed only where the permanent establishment (PE) sits.
Goods stored and shipped from FBA warehouses do not create a PE under Article 9, paragraph 3(b).
Keep no US office, no US employees and no agent in the US who negotiates or signs contracts.
Amazon collects marketplace sales tax.

cards.head: Ownership
items: Lucy owns 100%. Mark is paid under a written consulting or commission agreement.
If Mark became an owner the LLC would be a partnership: Form 1065 and 37% withholding on her share of profit.
Alternative kept open: Mark's own US company as distributor and importer of record, with Lucy at the wholesale layer.

s13.notes: Wyoming is cheap, private and has no state income tax; Delaware only pays off if investors arrive. The two things that keep US tax to zero are the treaty PE rule and discipline about who signs contracts. Form 5472 is the filing people forget and the penalty is {penalty_5472}, so it goes on the compliance calendar on day one.

s19.title: Day 90 gate and kill criteria

d90_rows.metric: Unit session conversion on 3 of 5 launch SKUs
TACOS in Month 3, falling month over month
Contribution per unit before advertising on 3 of 5 SKUs
Cash runway after funding the next PO

m12_rows.pass: positive two months in a row
m12_rows.kill: three negative months with a funding gap above {gt_m12_gap_kill}

s19.rule: KILL if any kill trigger fires. PASS if every threshold is met. REVIEW otherwise: fix and retest within 30 days. Kill means no further capital, sell down inventory, delist losers, move to Plan B.
s19.notes: The gate numbers are written down before the first purchase order so nobody argues with them later. Any single kill trigger kills; passing needs every threshold. The Low case reads {gate_d90_L} at Day 90 and {gate_m12_L} at Month 12, which is the point: the model itself says when to stop.
